The International Foundation Year in Nursing provides a strong foundation for students looking to pursue a career in healthcare.

This programme is designed to help students build the essential academic and English language skills needed to begin their nursing degree at Edinburgh Napier University. It provides a strong foundation in healthcare-related subjects, preparing them for success in both their studies and future professional practice.
7k0q:
The International Stage One (IS1) represents the first year of a four-year undergraduate degree which caters specifically for the needs of international students. It provides an opportunity for students to take part in a bespoke programme which maps against the standard first year offered at Edinburgh Napier University (ENU). They will be able to study in the supportive environment of an international college situated on an ENU campus and follow a Learning, Teaching and Assessment Approach designed to meet their learning needs while still being immersed in a university environment, accessing University facilities and resources and following university undergraduate regulations. Successful completion of the IS1 enables them to join the second year of their undergraduate studies at Edinburgh Napier University.

During students' studies on International Stage One (IS1) they will enhance their English language capabilities, develop academic study skills appropriate to the United Kingdom Higher Education environment and acclimate to living and studying in another country and cultural context very different from their own. Alongside language and study skills tuition, those working on the International Stage One are also able to study content modules within a chosen field of study and which are closely related to modules delivered in Edinburgh Napier University (ENU)’s standard year one. They are therefore able to join their second year studies at Scottish Credit and Qualifications Framework (SCQF) Level 8 alongside continuing students with increased confidence in both their language and study skills and subject knowledge.

The Bachelor of Science (Honours) Applied Microbiology course provides students with specialist skills in food, medical and environmental microbiology and biotechnology while also giving them a broad understanding of the biological sciences.

6tbn: The one term IIM pathway allows student to build on earlier studies in higher education in own country or elsewhere and so prepare yourself for study on an appropriate taught masters at Edinburgh Napier University. You also enhance your English language capabilities, develop graduate study skills appropriate to the UK Higher Education environment and acclimatise to living and studying in another country and a cultural context very different from your own.
6tb2:
The one term International Incorporated Masters pathway allows student to build on earlier studies in higher education in own country or elsewhere and so prepare themselves for study on an appropriate taught masters at Edinburgh Napier University. Student also enhance their English language capabilities, develop graduate study skills appropriate to the United Kingdom Higher Education environment and acclimatize to living and studying in another country and a cultural context very different from their own.

This pathway offers a blend of content modules with a clear focus on subject areas related to student's destination master’s programme with language and academic study skills tuition. The content modules are normally set at Levels 7, 8 and 10 and those working towards completion of the pathway are able to acquire 60 credits in a term of study. If they successfully complete the pathway, they will have met the requirements set by the University and are able to move onto your chosen master’s programme increased confidence in both language and study skills and subject knowledge.
